content_html_sanitized:
Source: http://www.marijuananews.com

Posted July 28, 2000
Special to MarijuanaNews by Richard Cowan

Today the Federal government continued its war on the sick, dying and disabled by seeking an emergency stay of Judge Breyer’s ruling that patients who meet certain criteria have a right to access to medical marijuana.
See
What Hath Breyer Wrought?
The Debate Over the Medical Necessity Ruling. Analysis by Richard Cowan

The 9th Circuit will almost certainly announce its ruling on the stay within a week. It seems unlikely that they would stay a ruling that was made on their instructions. When the government asked the entire 9th Circuit to hear an appeal of the ruling by the 3 judge panel, not a single judge on the entire 9th Circuit voted to hear the appeal.
See
Major Victory For Medical Marijuana In California:
9th Circuit Court Of Appeals Denies Clinton Administration's
Petition For Rehearing And Rehearing En Banc!

In addition to seeking the stay, the Feds are also seeking a fast-track ruling by the Supreme Court that might speed up the appeals process by a year. They have also filed the standard appeal of Breyer’s ruling back to the 9th Circuit, but obviously they don’t expect a favorable outcome from that.

Because the government’s attacks on the Oakland CBC have been civil rather than criminal, it was the DEAland Solicitor General who filed a petition of certiorari asking the Supreme Court to review the Ninth Circuit's ruling that instructed Breyer to reverse himself.

Only about 1% of certiorari writs are granted, so it seems unlikely that the Supreme Court will accept the Feds’ petition, especially inasmuch as there are no conflicting appellate court decisions. It is expected to be several months before the Supreme Court announces its decision on whether to grant certiorari. They do not meet again until October. Consequently, it seems very unlikely that there could be a ruling by the High Court in less than a year. Two years would be a better guess.

Nonetheless, this is obviously a very important issue for the Feds. The decision to seek the stay and the certiorari petition was made at the highest level of the DEAland government.
See
Was The Decision To Prosecute B. E. Smith Made At The White House?
The Key Question About The Selective Prosecution Of Medical Marijuana Activists.
Analysis -- By Richard Cowan

My sources tell me that when the Solicitor General was asked about the case at a private meeting, he said that the government had to act fast or there would be a proliferation of medical marijuana clubs.

It was clear that he was very familiar with the case, but when asked the basis of the government’s appeal, he said that they would argue the science.

This statement raises serious questions about his depth of understanding of the issue. For one thing, the government has never won an argument about medical marijuana on the merits.
See
The Party Line Versus Reality On Medical Marijuana.
Prohibitionism Is Being Destroyed By Its Own Delusions.
Analysis By Richard Cowan and 1 Article
and
California Nurses Association -- Representing 30,000 Registered Nurses --
Urges Judge Breyer Not to Wait For Appeals Court Ruling;
Allow Oakland Club to Distribute Medical Marijuana Now!
Special to Marijuananews

Perhaps for that reason, they never raised the scientific issues in the 9th Circuit. Instead, they simply kept saying that the Congress had voted that marijuana has no medical value, and that is sufficient to justify leaving the sick and dying to suffer without redress.

The appellate court, in its September ruling, found the government had failed to rebut evidence that cannabis is the only effective treatment for a large group of seriously ill patients. At the most recent hearing, when the government failed to offer any new arguments showing why it would not be in the public's interest to exempt some patients from federal narcotics laws, Breyer said, " As a result of the government's failure to offer any new evidence in opposition to defendants' motion, and in light of the 9th Circuit's opinion, the court must conclude that modifying the injunction as requested is in the public interest and exercise its equitable discretion to do so. "

Because the government never argued the " science " in the original case, they cannot raise any such issues in the appeal. That means that the government’s case will simply be that the sick and dying – who face imminent harm and have no alternatives to medical marijuana -- must nonetheless be deprived of the only thing that alleviates their suffering, or even saves their lives, simply because the Congress more or less said so. That is going to be a tough argument. Moreover, as the Solicitor General observed, there will be a lot more people involved by the time the High Court rules.

Off course, no matter who wins the November elections, there will be a whole new set of players in the government next year, so someone else will have to argue the case when it finally makes it to the High Court.

George W. Bush has said that he thinks that medical marijuana is a matter for the states, so he might drop the appeal. Gore’s latest position is the same as the Clinton Administration’s.
See
Even The Washington Post Notices As " Gore Reverses Stance On Medical Marijuana " Getting Worse.

(Nader’s position is mumble, mumble, mumble. Buchanan’s position is that heterosexuals of European ancestry can have all the marijuana they want as long as they smoke it in a closet. Or something like that.

Of course, Harry Browne, the Libertarian, is simply in favor of legalizing marijuana.)
